passage: Seema here, from the next bench. In the cloakroom after games, I watched Aadhya do up her shirt. She pushed each button in and then looked down. The collar sat lower on one side and the hem hung longer. She tugged at it, then undid every button with slow fingers and began again at the lowest button. This time the holes and buttons matched. She smoothed the front flat. She did not ask anyone for help. I cannot say what she was thinking, but she looked satisfied.

qa.q: Where did Aadhya begin again after she undid the shirt?
qa.a: Aadhya began again at the lowest button.

qa.q: What might Aadhya be feeling as she tugs at the crooked shirt?
qa.a: She may be annoyed at the mistake but determined to fix it. Seema cannot be sure, since undoing every button was slow and careful.

qa.q: What could Aadhya do next time to avoid crooked buttons, and why?
qa.a: She could line up the bottom button first from the start, or check in a mirror. Starting from the bottom shows sooner if the row is right.

qa.q: How does the redoing look to Seema?
qa.a: Seema sees Aadhya spot the mistake and fix it calmly, without asking anyone. Seema is left unsure what Aadhya was thinking.

grounding: A child does the buttons one hole out, sees the crooked shirt, undoes it and starts again from the bottom button.

passage:
Monday: Farida buttoned her school shirt one hole out and went to school crooked. Jyoti, her sister, laughed.
Wednesday: she buttoned it, looked in the mirror, and saw one side hanging lower. She undid every button and started again from the bottom one.
Friday: she began at the bottom, checked the mirror at the top and smiled.

qa.q: Where did Farida start on Wednesday?
qa.a: She started again from the bottom one.

qa.q: What was Farida feeling on Monday when Jyoti laughed?
qa.a: She was probably embarrassed at going to school crooked.
Match the top button to the top hole first, so both ends line up.

qa.q: How might Jyoti see Farida's fix?
qa.a: Jyoti may be impressed that her sister spotted and fixed it herself.

grounding: Over several days a child notices her shirt hanging crooked from misaligned buttons and learns to start again from the bottom.

passage: The school van would honk in five minutes. Abhinav buttoned his shirt fast, but one side hung lower. His brother Farhan, putting on shoes, pointed. "You're crooked." Abhinav looked down, groaned, undid every button and started from the bottom. The van honked just as he did the top. "Straight!" he said, running out.

qa.q: How long until the van honked?
What was Abhinav feeling when he groaned?
qa.a: He was frustrated and worried about being late.

qa.q: What else could Abhinav do when time is short?
qa.a: Start from the bottom button every time, so he gets it right the first time.

qa.q: How does Abhinav's fix look to Farhan?
qa.a: Farhan sees his brother fix it quickly and make the van in time.

grounding: A child sees his shirt hanging crooked, undoes the buttons and starts from the bottom, fixing the mistake.
